title: API Family Delivery Specification: chat/completions/embeddings/rerank — requirements, scope changes, and launch rundown
creator: Aisha Patel
description: This ticket is the canonical PRD and launch readiness checklist for the hosted API family delivering chat, completions, embeddings, and a rerank capability as a cohesive surface. It consolidates functional requirements, clarified scope after recent trade-offs, measurable acceptance criteria, and a sequenced launch checklist with canary/rollout guidance. Goal: ship a single, predictable API suite that supports developer-friendly defaults, per-endpoint SLAs, cost-control knobs (batching/kv caching), and a clear rollback path. This doc focuses on the delivery contract for hosted customers and handoff items for Dedicated/Private as needed.
requirements: Unified API surface: single /v1/generate and /v1/embeddings endpoints with explicit type param for chat/completion mode and an opt-in rerank route; backward-compatible aliases maintained for legacy clients.

SDK parity: JS/Python SDKs expose identical method signatures, streaming support for chat & completions, and a high-level rerank helper that accepts candidate lists and returns ranked ids with scores.

Performance targets: P50 token latency < 70ms for short prompts (<=128 tokens) on hosted S1 models; P95 < 200ms. Embeddings: P99 < 150ms for 1-4 inputs. Rerank throughput: support 2500 candidate evaluations/sec per allocation.
Reliability: 99.95% availability for hosted endpoints with automatic fallback to smaller model variants when capacity or quota limits are hit.
Cost controls: default server-side batching enabled for multi-request workloads, configurable batching window per API key, and documentation of cost/latency tradeoffs.

Security & privacy: all requests logged with token-level cost metadata; customer data in hosted mode retained for 30 days by default with opt-out. KMS integration required for dedicated/private integrations (see ENG dependency).
Observability: per-route dashboards, request sampling for traces, per-key token cost breakdowns, and regression alerts tied to evaluation prompt sets.
Acceptance test harness: end-to-end test suites in CI that validate correctness for deterministic prompts, streaming order integrity, and rerank stability on seeding datasets.
Rollout controls: canary targeting by API key, region, and plan with automatic rollback on defined SLO regressions.
out_of_scope: Self-hosted deployment packaging — Private/Dedicated install artifacts are handled in a separate project; this ticket only defines API contracts for compatibility.
Custom model fine-tuning pipeline — not part of hosted endpoint initial launch, will be considered post-MVP.
Language-specific SDKs beyond JS/Python for initial launch (Go/Rust scheduled in next cycle).
scope_changes: 2025-02-20: Removed inline synchronous rerank from /v1/generate path — introduced dedicated /v1/rerank endpoint to simplify latency SLAs and caching semantics. Decision: improves isolation of compute patterns and enables separate autoscaling.
2025-02-27: Deferred multi-tenant per-request KV-cache pinning to post-launch due to runtime integration complexity (moved to ENG-41820).

2025-03-03: Reduced streaming window default from 250ms to 100ms after QA latency regressions; added explicit SDK opt-in for 'aggressiveStreaming' to avoid surprising cost changes for low-volume users.
acceptance_criteria: API contract: OpenAPI spec published and validated by SDK generation tooling; no breaking changes vs agreed alias mappings.
Performance: Verified in staging with production-like traffic that P50 and P95 latency targets are met for the S1 model family across regions (benchmarks attached).
Stability: End-to-end error rate < 0.5% during a 24-hour stability run with randomized prompt corpus; no data loss on streaming connections longer than 30s.
Security: KMS integration smoke test green and data-retention config enforced for hosted accounts; security review signoff received.
Observability: Dashboards and regression alerts configured; alert playbooks documented and reviewed by on-call rotation.
Docs & SDKs: Public docs (API reference, migration guide, cost guidance) published; JS/Python SDKs have release candidates and integration tests pass.
Rollout: Canary passes defined SLO gates for 72 hours before extending to 50% of traffic; automated rollback works end-to-end.

rollout_plan: Week 0: internal dogfooding and integration tests. Week 1: 1% canary (internal + selected customers) for 72h with automated SLO monitoring. Week 2: extend to 25% if canary healthy, monitor cost signals; enable additional regions. Week 3: broad rollout to GA if acceptance gates hold. At every step, feature flags allow disabling streaming or rerank. Rollback path documented to redirect traffic to legacy endpoint aliases and smaller model family.
qa_notes: Create deterministic seed corpus (1k prompts) that includes streaming edge cases and long-running completions.
Include fuzzing for rerank inputs (duplicate IDs, empty candidate lists, malformed scores).
Validate SDK streaming order using sequence IDs and simulate flaky network conditions.
Run cost smoke tests to ensure batching does not cause token overcount regressions.
